zh: 刘不才却对他的话大感兴趣，『这倒是个办法。』他说，『照我看，那批人又想吃羊肉，又怕羊骚臭；怕将来官军光复了，跟他们算帐。如果真的有保护他们的把握，那批人肯照我们的办法做的。不过，空口说白话可不行。』『现在当然只有空口说白话；话要动听，能够做得到，他们自然会相信。』胡雪岩停了一下说∶『三叔，这件事只有你辛苦，再去一趟∶因为别人去说，他们不大容易相信。』『这还用说？自然是我去。你说，跟他们怎么个讲法。』『当然要吹点牛。』胡雪岩停了下来∶『等我好好想一想。』这一想想了好多时候，或者是暂且丢开此事；总而言之，不见他再谈起，尽自问着杭州的情形，琐琐屑屑，无不关怀。雪岩的交游甚广，但问起熟人，不是殉难，就是下落不明，存者十不得一。连不相干的古应春，都听得凄怆不止。
en: Liu, however, was greatly interested. “That might work,” he said. “As I see it, they want to eat the mutton without enduring its smell. They are afraid that, once the government troops recover the city, they will be called to account. If you really can protect them, they will be willing to do as we ask. But mere words will not suffice.” “For the moment, words are all we have. If the offer appeals to them and is something we can fulfil, they will believe it.” Hu paused. “Third Uncle, I must trouble you to make another journey. They would find it harder to believe anyone else.” “Of course I shall go. What shall I say to them?” “A little boasting will be necessary.” Hu broke off. “Let me think it over properly.” He thought for a long time—or perhaps put the matter aside for the moment. At any rate, he said no more about it. Instead he asked about Hangzhou, showing concern for every trifling detail. He had a wide acquaintance, but of the people he asked after, most had died in the calamity or vanished without trace. Fewer than one in ten were known to have survived. Even Gu, who had no personal connection with them, listened in deep distress.

zh: 到得十点多种，刘不才一路车船劳顿，又是说话没有停过，再好的精神也支持不住了。古应春例劝他不必再住客栈，先好好睡一觉再说；刘不才依从，由古家的丫头侍候着，上床休息。
en: After ten o’clock, the strain of the journey by land and water, followed by so much uninterrupted talking, had exhausted even Liu’s vigorous constitution. Gu urged him to forget about returning to the inn and get a good night’s rest first. Liu agreed. A maid of the household attended to him, and he went to bed.

zh: 胡雪岩的精神却还很好，『老古，』他招招手让古应春坐在床前，低声说道∶『我对人不用不光明的手段，这一次要做它一次一百零一回的买卖，全家大小在那班王八蛋手里，不能不防他们一着。我现在要埋一条药线在那里；好便好，搞得不好，我点上药线轰他娘的，教他们也不得安逸。话说明了，你心里也有数了；要劳你的神，替我做一件公事。』他是『话说明了』，古应春却如丈二金刚摸不着头脑，『小爷叔，』他皱着眉说，『我还莫名其妙；什么药线，什么公事？』
en: Hu was still full of energy. “Gu,” he said, beckoning his friend to sit by the bed, “I do not use underhand methods against people. This time I must make an exception. My whole family is in the hands of those bastards; I cannot afford to leave myself unprotected. I intend to lay a fuse. If all goes well, well and good. If it does not, I shall light it and blast the devils out of their comfort. Now that I have explained, you know what is in my mind. I need you to take some trouble over an official dispatch for me.” He might consider himself to have explained, but Gu was utterly bewildered. “Little Uncle,” he said, frowning, “I still have no idea what you mean. What fuse? What official dispatch?”

zh: 『公事就是药线，药线就是公事。』胡雪岩说∶『这件公事，是以我浙江候补道兼团练局委员，奉王抚台委派，筹划浙江军需民食，以及地方赈济事宜的身分，报给闽浙总督衙门庆制军。公事上要说明，王雪公生前就顾虑援兵不到，杭州恐怕保不住，特意嘱咐我，他是决定城亡人亡，一死报答朝廷；但是杭州的百姓，不可不顾，因为我不是地方官，并无守土之责，所以，万一杭州沦陷，必得顾念家乡，想办法保护地方百姓。这是第一段。』古应春很仔细地听着，已理会得胡雪岩入手的意思，并即说道∶『第二段当然是叙你运粮到杭州，不能进城的情形？』『对！不过转道宁波这一层不必提。』胡雪岩略停一下又说，『现在要叙顶要紧的第三段，要这样说法∶我因为人在上海，不能回杭州，已经派人跟某某人、某某人联络，请他们保护地方百姓，并且暗中布置，以便官军一到，可以相机策应。这批人都是地方公正士绅，秉心忠义，目前身陷城中，不由自主；将来收复杭州，不但不能论他们在长毛那里干过什么职司，而且要大大地奖励他们。』『啊，啊！』古应春深深点头，『我懂了，我懂了，这就是替他们的将来留个退步。』
en: “The dispatch is the fuse, and the fuse is the dispatch,” Hu replied. “It is to be addressed to Governor-General Qing at the office of the governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang. I shall write in my capacity as a circuit intendant awaiting appointment in Zhejiang and a member of the militia bureau, commissioned by Governor Wang to arrange military supplies, food for the people, and local relief. Begin by explaining that, before his death, Mr Xuexuan feared that reinforcements might not arrive and Hangzhou might prove impossible to hold. He expressly charged me with this duty: he himself was determined to die with the city and repay the court with his life, but the people of Hangzhou must not be abandoned. I held no local administrative post and bore no responsibility for defending the territory. Therefore, should Hangzhou fall, I must remember my native place and find ways of protecting its people. That is the first section.” Gu listened closely and began to understand how Hu meant to proceed. “The second section will presumably describe your attempt to bring rice to Hangzhou and your inability to enter the city?” “Exactly. But there is no need to mention the diversion to Ningbo.” Hu paused briefly. “Now comes the third and most important section. It must say this: since I am in Shanghai and cannot return to Hangzhou, I have sent someone to contact such-and-such persons, asking them to protect the inhabitants and secretly prepare to assist the government troops when a favourable opportunity arises upon their arrival. These men are all upright local gentlemen, loyal at heart. At present they are trapped in the city and cannot act freely. When Hangzhou is recovered, whatever offices they may have held under the rebels must not be counted against them. On the contrary, they should be generously rewarded.” “Ah!” Gu nodded deeply. “I understand. You are leaving them a way out for the future.”

zh: 『对了。这道公事要等庆制军的批示，他人在福州，一时办不到；所以要来个变通办法，一方面呈报庆制军，一方面请江苏巡抚衙门代咨闽浙总督衙门，同时给我个复文，拿我的原文都叙在里头，我好给他们看。』『嗯、嗯！』古应春想了一下，记起一句话∶『那么什么叫「公事就是药线」呢？』『这你还不懂？』胡雪岩提醒他说∶『你先从相机策应官军这句话上去想，就懂了。』真所谓『光棍一点就透』，古应春恍然大悟，如果那批人不肯就范，甚至真个不利于胡家眷属；胡雪岩就可用这件公事作为报复，向长毛告密，说这班人勾结清军，江苏巡抚衙门的回文，便是铁证。那一来，后果就可想而知了。这一着实在狠。但原是为了报复，甚至可以作为防卫；如果那批人了解到这道公事是是一根一点便可轰发火药，炸得粉身碎骨的药线，自然不敢轻举妄动。『小爷叔！』古应春赞叹着说『真正「死棋肚子里出仙着」；这一着，亏你怎么想出来的？』
en: “Precisely. We ought to wait for Governor-General Qing’s endorsement, but he is in Fuzhou and that cannot be obtained quickly. So we must improvise. While submitting the report to him, I shall also ask the governor of Jiangsu to forward an official communication to his office and give me a reply reciting my original report in full. I can then show it to those men.” Gu reflected. “But what did you mean when you said the dispatch was the fuse?” “Do you still not see? Think about the passage concerning assistance to the government troops.” A hint was enough for a man as shrewd as Gu. If those people refused to cooperate, or actually harmed Hu’s family, Hu could retaliate with this very dispatch. He could inform the rebels that the men were in league with the Qing forces, producing the reply from the governor of Jiangsu as conclusive evidence. The consequences were easy to imagine. It was a ruthless move. But it was intended for retaliation, and might serve as protection in itself. If the men understood that the dispatch was a fuse which, once lit, could blow them to pieces, they would not dare act rashly. “Little Uncle,” Gu exclaimed in admiration, “you have found a brilliant move in a position that looked completely lost! How did you think of it?”

zh: 『也不是我发明的。我不过拿人家用过的办法，变通一下子。说起来，还要谢谢王雪公，他讲过一个故事给我听；这个故事出在他们家乡，康熙年间有位李中堂，据说在福建名气大得很，他的同年陈翰林跟他有段生死不解的仇——。』王有龄告诉胡雪岩的故事如此∶这位李中堂是福建安溪人，他的同年陈翰林是福州人。这年翰林散馆，两个人请假结伴回乡。不久就有三藩之乱，耿精忠响应吴三桂，在福州也叛变了，开府设官，陈翰林被迫受了伪职。李中堂见猎心喜，也想到福州讨个一官半职。而陈翰林却看出耿精忠恐怕不成气候，便劝李中堂不必如此。而且两个人闭门密谈，定下一计，由李中堂写下一道密疏，指陈方略，请朝廷速派大兵入闽。这道密疏封在蜡丸之中，由李家派人取道江西入京，请同乡代为奏达御前。
en: “I did not invent it. I have merely adapted a method used before. In fact, I owe Mr Xuexuan my thanks. He once told me a story from his own province. In the Kangxi reign there was a Minister Li, a very famous man in Fujian, apparently. A fellow graduate of his, Hanlin Academician Chen, became his sworn enemy.” This was the story Wang had told him. Minister Li came from Anxi in Fujian; Academician Chen came from Fuzhou. When their period of training at the Hanlin Academy ended, the two took leave and travelled home together. Not long afterwards came the Revolt of the Three Feudatories. Geng Jingzhong responded to Wu Sangui’s call and rebelled in Fuzhou, establishing an administration and appointing officials. Chen was compelled to accept an office under him. Li saw the opportunity with keen interest and also wanted to seek a post in Fuzhou. Chen, however, doubted that Geng’s venture would succeed and advised him against it. The two then closeted themselves together and devised a plan. Li would write a secret memorial setting out a strategy and urging the court to send a large army into Fujian at once. The memorial was sealed in a pellet of wax. A messenger from Li’s household carried it through Jiangxi to the capital, where a fellow provincial was asked to submit it to the emperor.

zh: 『这是「刀切豆腐两面光」的打算。』胡雪岩说∶『李中堂与陈翰林约定，如果朝廷大兵到福建，耿精忠垮台，李中堂当然就是大大的功臣，那时候他就可以替陈翰林洗刷，说他投贼完全是为了要打探机密，策应官军——。』『啊、啊，妙！如果耿精忠成了功，李中堂这首密疏，根本没有人知道；陈翰林依旧可以保荐他成为新贵。是不是这样的打算？』『一点不错。』『那末后来呢？』古应春很感兴趣地问∶『怎么说是成了生死不解的冤家？』『就为李中堂不是东西，出卖朋友。耿精忠垮台，朝廷收复福建，要办叛逆的罪；李中堂自己得意了，竟不替他洗刷。害得陈翰林充军到关外。』胡雪岩说，『我现在仿照他们的办法，但愿那批人很识相，我替他们留下的这条洗刷的路子，将来一定有用。』『对！小爷叔的意思，我完全懂了；这道公事我连夜替你预备起来。』
en: “They meant to come out well whichever side won,” Hu continued. “Li and Chen agreed that, if the imperial troops entered Fujian and Geng fell, Li would of course have performed a great service. He could then clear Chen’s name, explaining that Chen had joined the rebels solely to discover their secrets and assist the government forces—” “Ah, excellent! And if Geng succeeded, no one would know of Li’s secret memorial. Chen could still recommend him for a fine position under the new regime. Was that the plan?” “Exactly.” “What happened afterwards, then?” Gu asked with interest. “How did they become mortal enemies?” “Because Li was a scoundrel who betrayed his friend. Geng fell, the court recovered Fujian, and the rebels were to be punished. Li, secure in his own success, did nothing to clear Chen, who was sent into military exile beyond the pass.” Hu went on, “I am now borrowing their method. I only hope those people have the sense to cooperate. The means of clearing their names that I am providing will certainly be useful to them one day.” “I understand your intentions completely, Little Uncle. I shall prepare the dispatch for you tonight.”

zh: 『不忙。明天动笔也不迟。』胡雪岩说，『我还有件事要先跟你商量。』这件事是为王有龄身后打算，自不外名利两字。王有龄的宦囊虽不太丰，却决不能说是一清如水∶『三年清知府，十万雪花银』，许多收入象征粮的『羡余』；漕粮折实，碎角子熔铸为五十两银子一个的『官宝』，照例要加收的『火耗』，在雍正年间就已『化暗为明』，明定为地方官的『养廉银』。此外『三节两寿』——过年、端午、中秋三节；本人及太太的两个生日，属员必有馈敬，而且数目亦大致有定规，这都是朝廷所许的收入。
en: “There is no hurry. Tomorrow will be soon enough,” Hu said. “There is something else I must discuss with you first.” This concerned provision for Wang after his death: his reputation and his property. His savings from office were not exceptionally large, but neither could it be said that he had taken nothing. As the saying went, even an honest prefect might save a hundred thousand taels in three years. Officials had many sources of income, including surpluses from grain taxation and the customary allowance for wastage when small pieces of silver, collected in commutation of tribute grain, were melted down into official ingots weighing fifty taels each. In the Yongzheng reign, such receipts had been brought into the open and formally designated as allowances for the maintenance of integrity. There were also gifts at the New Year, the Dragon Boat Festival, and the Mid-Autumn Festival, and on the birthdays of the official and his wife. Subordinates invariably sent them, in amounts largely fixed by custom. These were all forms of income permitted by the court.

zh: 王有龄的积蓄，当然是交给胡雪岩营运；他现在要跟古应春商议的，就因为经手的款子，要有个交代。『他们说王雪公有钱在我手里，这是当然的。我跟死者的交情，当然也不会「起黑心」。不过，』说到这里，他有点烦躁，『这样的局面，放出去的款子；摆下去的本钱，一时哪里去回笼？真教我不好交代。』这确是极为难的事。古应春的想法比胡雪岩还要深，王有龄已经殉节，遗属不少，眼前居家度日，将来男婚女嫁，不但在在要钱，而且有了钱也不能坐吃山空。所以，他说∶『你还不能只顾眼前的交代，要替王家筹个久长之计才好。』『这倒没有什么好筹划的，反正只要胡雪岩一家有饭吃；决不会让王家吃粥，我愁的是眼前！』胡雪岩说∶『王雪公跟我的交情，可以说他就是我，我就是他。他在天之灵，一定会谅解我的处境。不过王太太或者不晓得我的心，他家的亲友更加隔膜，只知道有钱在我这里，不知道这笔钱一时收不回来。现在外头既有这样的闲话，我如果不能拿白花花的现银子捧出来，人家只当我欺侮孤儿寡妇。这个名声，你想想，我怎么吃得消？』
en: Wang’s savings had naturally been entrusted to Hu for investment. What Hu now needed to discuss was how to account for the money that had passed through his hands. “They say I have Mr Xuexuan’s money. Of course I have. With the friendship there was between us, I would never dream of keeping it dishonestly. But”—he grew agitated—“in a situation like this, how can I call in loans and recover invested capital at a moment’s notice? I truly do not know how to settle matters.” It was indeed a serious difficulty. Gu’s thoughts went further. Wang had died for his duty and left a sizeable family. They needed money for their immediate living expenses and, later, to marry off the children. Even if they received the money, they could not simply live on their capital until it was exhausted. “You must think beyond settling the account now,” he said. “You ought to make lasting provision for the Wang family.” “There is not much to plan there. So long as the Hu family has rice to eat, I shall never let the Wangs live on gruel. It is the immediate problem that worries me. Mr Xuexuan and I were so close that he was as much myself as I was. His spirit in Heaven will understand my predicament. But Mrs Wang may not know what is in my heart; her relatives and friends will understand even less. All they know is that I hold this money, not that I cannot recover it at once. Since such rumours are already abroad, unless I can produce the shining silver itself, people will say I am taking advantage of a widow and orphans. Think what that would do to my reputation!”

zh: 古应春觉得这个看法不错，他也是熟透人情世故的人，心里又有进一步的想法∶如果胡雪岩将王有龄名下的款子，如数交付，王家自然信任他，继续托他营运，手里仍可活动。否则，王家反倒有些不大放心，会要求收回。既然如此，就乐得做得漂亮些。麻烦的是，杭州一陷，上海的生意又一时不能抽本，无法做得『漂亮』。那就要靠大家帮忙了。『小爷叔，』他问∶『王雪公有多少款子在你手里？』『王太太手里有帐的，大概有十万；另外还有两万在云南，不知道王太太知道不知道。』『那就奇怪了。怎么在云南会有两万银子？』
en: Gu thought this sound reasoning. He too understood human nature thoroughly, and carried the argument a step further. If Hu handed over the entire sum belonging to Wang, the family would naturally trust him and ask him to continue investing it, leaving it at his disposal. Otherwise they might become uneasy and insist on withdrawing it. Given that, he might as well make a handsome job of it. The trouble was that Hangzhou had fallen, while the capital invested in Shanghai could not be withdrawn immediately. A handsome settlement was therefore impossible without help from their friends. “Little Uncle, how much of Mr Xuexuan’s money do you have?” “Mrs Wang has the accounts. About a hundred thousand taels. There are another twenty thousand in Yunnan, though I do not know whether she knows about those.” “How strange! How did twenty thousand taels come to be in Yunnan?”

zh: 『是这样子的，』胡雪岩说，『咸丰六年冬天，何根云交卸浙江巡抚，王雪公在浙江的官，也没有什么做头了；事先安排，调补云南粮道。我替他先汇了两万银子到云南。后来何根云调升两江，王雪公自然跟到江苏；云南的两万银子始终未动，存在昆明钱庄是生息。王雪公始终不忘云南，生前跟我说过，有机会很想做一任云南巡抚；能做到云贵总督，当然更好。这两万银子在云南迟早有用处，不必去动它。现在，当然再也用不着了！』说到这里，胡雪岩又生感触，泫然欲涕。
en: “This is how it happened,” Hu said. “In the winter of the sixth year of Xianfeng, He Genyun left his post as governor of Zhejiang, and Mr Xuexuan had little prospect of making a career there any longer. Arrangements had already been made for him to become grain intendant in Yunnan. I remitted twenty thousand taels there in advance. Afterwards He was promoted to governor-general of Liangjiang, and Mr Xuexuan naturally followed him to Jiangsu. The twenty thousand in Yunnan were never touched; they remained on deposit with a bank in Kunming, earning interest. Mr Xuexuan never forgot Yunnan. He used to tell me that, given the opportunity, he would very much like to serve a term as governor there. Better still if he could become governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou. Sooner or later, he said, the money would be useful in Yunnan, so we need not withdraw it. Now, of course, he will never need it again.” At this, emotion overcame Hu once more, and tears rose to his eyes.

zh: 等他拭一拭眼睛，擤一擤鼻子，情绪略略平伏，古应春便接着话题顺∶『款子放在钱庄里，总有折子；折子在谁手里？』『麻烦就在这里。折子是有一个，我交了给王雪公；大概是他弄掉了，也记不起这回事，反来问我。这原是无所谓的事；跟他们再补一个就是。后来事多，一直搁着未办；如今人已过世，倒麻烦了，只怕对方不肯承认。』『你是原经手。』古应春说，『似乎跟王雪公在世还是故世，不生关系。不过，钱庄的规矩，我也不大懂，不知道麻烦何在？』『钱庄第一讲信用；第二讲关系；第三才讲交情。云南这家同业，信用并不见得好；交情也谈不上；唯一讲得上的，就是关系。王雪公在日，现任的巡抚，云南方面说得上话；我自己呢，阜康在上海的生意不算大，浙江已经坐第一把交椅，云南有协饷之类的公款往来，我可以照应他们，论生意上的关系也够。不过，现在不同了，他们未见得再肯买帐。』这番分析，极其透彻。古应春听入心头，亦颇有感慨；如今做生意要想发展，似乎不是靠官场的势力关系，就得沾洋人的光。风气如此，夫复何言？看起来王有龄那笔款子，除非大有力者援手，恐怕要『泡汤』了。
en: Gu waited while he wiped his eyes, blew his nose, and recovered some composure, then resumed the discussion. “Money deposited with a bank must have a passbook. Who has it?” “That is the difficulty. There was a passbook, and I gave it to Mr Xuexuan. I suppose he lost it and forgot about it, for he later asked me where it was. It did not seem to matter at the time. We could simply ask them for a replacement. Then other business intervened, and it was left undone. Now that he is dead, it becomes troublesome. I fear they may refuse to acknowledge the deposit.” “You handled the original transaction,” Gu said. “Whether Mr Xuexuan is alive or dead would seem to make no difference. But I do not know much about banking customs. Where is the difficulty?” “For a bank, credit comes first, business connections second, and personal friendship only third. This Yunnan bank’s credit is not particularly good, and there is no friendship to speak of. The only thing we could count on was influence through our connections. While Mr Xuexuan lived, he was a serving governor whose word carried weight in Yunnan. As for me, Fukang’s Shanghai business may be modest, but in Zhejiang we hold first place. Yunnan has transactions involving interprovincial military subsidies and other public funds, and I could help them with those. Our business connections should have been sufficient. But things have changed. They may no longer choose to oblige us.” The analysis was penetrating. Gu took it to heart, reflecting sadly that success in business nowadays seemed to depend either on official influence or on foreign connections. With things as they were, what more could be said? Unless someone very powerful intervened, Wang’s money might well be lost.

zh: 『只有这样，托出人来，请云贵总督，或者云南巡抚，派人去关照一声。念在王雪公为国殉难，遗属理当照应。或者那批大老肯出头管这个闲事。』『也只好这样。』胡雪岩说，『交涉归交涉，眼前我先要赔出来。』『这一来总数就是十二万。』古应春沉吟了一下，毅然决然地说∶『生意在一起，信用也是大家的。我想法子来替小爷叔凑足了就是。』这就是朋友的可贵了。胡雪岩心情很复杂，既感激，又不安；自觉不能因为古应春一肩承担，自己就可以置身事外，所以还是要问一问。
en: “There is only one course,” Gu said. “We must find an intermediary to ask the governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou, or the governor of Yunnan, to send someone to speak to the bank. Mr Xuexuan died for his country; his family deserves consideration. Perhaps one of those great men will consent to concern himself with the matter.” “That is all we can do,” Hu agreed. “But whatever negotiations we undertake, I must make up the money myself for the present.” “That makes a hundred and twenty thousand altogether.” Gu considered for a moment, then said resolutely, “We are in business together, and our credit is shared. I shall find a way to raise the full amount for you.” Here was the value of friendship. Hu felt both gratitude and unease. Gu’s willingness to bear the burden did not absolve him of responsibility. He still had to ask how it would be managed.

zh: 『老古，你肯帮我这个忙，我说感激的话，是多余的，不过，不能因为我，拖垮了你。十二万银子，到底也不是个小数目；我自己能凑多少，还不晓得，想来不过三五万。还有七八万，要现款，只怕不容易。『』那就跟小爷叔说实话，七八万现款，我一下子也拿不出；只有暂时调动一下，希望王太太只是过一过目，仍旧交给你放出去生息。『』嗯，嗯！『胡雪岩说，「这个打算办得到的。不过，也要防个万一。』『万一不成，只有硬挺。现在也顾不得那许多了。』胡雪岩点点头，自己觉得这件事总有八成把握，也就不再去多想；接下来谈到另一件事。
en: “Gu, words of gratitude are unnecessary between us. But I cannot let you ruin yourself on my account. A hundred and twenty thousand taels is no small sum. I do not yet know how much I can raise myself—perhaps thirty to fifty thousand at most. That still leaves seventy or eighty thousand. Finding that much ready cash will not be easy.” “To tell you the truth, Little Uncle, I cannot produce seventy or eighty thousand at once either. I can only move money around temporarily, in the hope that Mrs Wang will merely look at it and entrust it to you again to invest at interest.” “Yes,” Hu said. “I think that can be arranged. But we must allow for the possibility that it cannot.” “Then we shall simply have to hold on somehow. We cannot take every contingency into account now.” Hu nodded. He reckoned the plan had an eight-in-ten chance of success and thought no further about it. They turned to another matter.

zh: 『这件事，关系王雪公的千秋。』胡雪岩说，『听大书我也听得不少，忠臣也晓得几个；死得象王雪公这样惨的，实在不多。总要想办法替他表扬表扬，留下长远的纪念，才对得起死者。』『这又何劳你费心？朝廷表扬忠义，自然有一套恤典的。』朝廷的恤典，胡雪岩当然知道，象王有龄的这种情形，恤典必须优渥，除了照『巡抚例赐恤』，在赐谥、立传、赌祭以外，殉节的封疆大吏，照便可以入祀京师昭忠祠，子孙亦可获得云骑尉之类『世袭罔替』的『世职』。至于在本省及『立功省份』建立专祠，只要有人出面奏请，亦必可邀准，不在话下。
en: “This concerns Mr Xuexuan’s reputation through the ages,” Hu said. “I have heard plenty of storytellers and know of a few loyal ministers. Few died as cruelly as he did. We must find some way to honour him and leave a lasting memorial. Only then shall we have done our duty by him.” “Why should you have to trouble yourself over that? The court has its established honours for loyalty.” Hu knew this, of course. In a case such as Wang’s, the posthumous honours must be generous. Besides the customary provision for a deceased governor, there would be a posthumous title, an official biography, and sacrificial offerings. A high provincial official who died for his duty could customarily be honoured in the Shrine of Illustrious Loyalty in the capital. His descendants might receive a hereditary rank such as Yunqiwei, to be transmitted without reduction. As for a special shrine in his own province or in a province where he had performed distinguished service, approval was virtually assured if someone submitted the appropriate memorial.

zh: 胡雪岩的意思，却不是指这些例行的恤典，『我心里一直在想，王雪公死得冤枉！』他说，『想起他「死不瞑目」那句话，只怕我夜里都会睡不着觉。我要替他伸冤。至少，他生前的冤屈，要教大家晓得。』照胡雪岩的看法，王有龄的冤屈，不止一端∶第一、王履谦处处掣肘，宁绍可守而失守，以致杭州粮路断绝，陷入无可挽救的困境；第二，李元度做浙江的官，领浙江的饷，却在衡州逗留不进。如果他肯在浙西拼命猛攻，至少可以牵制浙西的长毛，杭州亦不会被重重围困得毫无生路；第三，两江总督曾国藩奉旨援浙而袖手旁观，大有见死不救之意，未免心狠。由于交情深厚，而且身历其境，同受荼毒，所以胡雪岩提到这些，情绪相当激动。而在古应春，看法却不尽相同；他的看法是就利害着眼，比较不涉感情。
en: But Hu was not thinking of these customary honours. “I cannot stop thinking how unjustly Mr Xuexuan died,” he said. “When I remember his words about being unable to close his eyes in peace, I doubt I shall ever sleep soundly. I want to obtain redress for him. At the very least, people must know the wrongs he suffered while alive.” In Hu’s view, there were several. First, Wang Lüqian had obstructed him at every turn. Ningbo and Shaoxing could have been held but were lost, cutting off Hangzhou’s food route and placing it in a hopeless position. Second, Li Yuandu held office in Zhejiang and drew his pay from Zhejiang, yet lingered in Hengzhou without advancing. Had he fought hard in western Zhejiang, he could at least have diverted the rebels there, and Hangzhou would not have been so completely surrounded. Third, Zeng Guofan, governor-general of Liangjiang, had received an imperial command to assist Zhejiang but stood by with folded arms, apparently willing to watch others perish. That was surely heartless. Hu spoke with considerable agitation. His friendship with Wang had been profound, and he himself had lived through the events and shared the suffering. Gu’s view was different. He considered consequences and interests, with less involvement of feeling.

zh: 『小爷叔，』古应春很冷静地问道∶『你是打算怎么样替王雪公伸冤？』『我有两个办法，第一是要请人做一篇墓志铭，拿死者的这些冤屈都叙上去；第二是花几吊银子，到京里请一位「都老爷」出面，狠狠参他一本。』『参哪个？』『参王履谦、李元度、还有两江的曾制台。』『我看难！』古应春说，『曾制台现在正大红大紫的时候，参他不倒。再说句良心话，人家远在安庆，救江苏还没有力量，哪里又分得出兵来救浙江？』
en: “Little Uncle,” Gu asked calmly, “how do you propose to seek redress?” “I have two plans. First, I shall ask someone to write an epitaph setting out all these wrongs. Second, I shall spend some money in the capital and get a censor to impeach them severely.” “Impeach whom?” “Wang Lüqian, Li Yuandu, and Governor-General Zeng of Liangjiang.” “I think that will be difficult,” Gu replied. “Governor-General Zeng is at the height of his favour. You will not bring him down by impeachment. Besides, in fairness, he is far away in Anqing and lacks even the strength to relieve Jiangsu. Where could he find troops to spare for Zhejiang?”

zh: 胡雪岩心里不以为然，但不愿跟古应春争执，『那末，王履谦、李元度呢？』他说，『这两个人总是罪有应得吧？』『王履廉是一定要倒霉的；李元度就说不定了。而且，现在兵荒马乱，路又不通，朝廷要彻查也无从查起。只有等将来局势平定了再说。』这一下惹得胡雪岩心头火发，咆哮着问∶『照你这样说，莫非就让这两个人逍遥法外？』胡雪岩从未有过这样的疾言厉色，古应春受惊发楞，好半天说不出话。那尴尬的脸色，亦是胡雪岩从未见过的；因而象镜子一样，使得他照见了自己的失态。『对不起，老古！』他低着头说，声音虽轻缓了许多；但仍掩不住他内心的愤慨不平。当然，这愤慨决不是对古应春。他觉得胡雪岩可怜亦可敬，然而却不愿说些胡雪岩爱听的话去安慰他。『小爷叔，我知道你跟王雪公的交情。不过，做事不能只讲感情，要讲是非利害。』这话胡雪岩自然同意，只一时想不出，在这件事上的是非利害是什么？一个人有了冤屈，难道连诉一诉苦都不能？然则何以叫『不平则鸣』？古应春见他不语，也就没有再说下去，其实他亦只是讲利害，未讲是非；这一阵子为了替胡雪岩打听杭州的消息，跟官场中人颇有往来，王有龄之殉节，以及各方面对杭州沦陷的感想批评，亦听了不少。大致说来，是同情王有龄的人多；但亦有人极力为曾国藩不救浙江辩护，其间党同伐异的论调，非常明显。王有龄孤军奋战，最有渊源的人，是何桂清，却是『泥菩萨过江，自身难保』。在这种情形之下，如果什么人要为王有龄打抱不平，争论是非，当然会触犯时忌；遭致不利，岂不太傻？古应春也知道自己的想法，庸俗卑下；但为了对胡雪岩的关切特甚，也就不能不从利害上去打算了。这些话一时说不透彻；而且最好是默喻而不必言传，他相信胡雪岩慢慢就会想明白，眼前最要紧的是筹划那十二万银子；以及替胡雪岩拟公文上闽浙总督。
en: Hu did not agree, but he had no wish to quarrel. “What about Wang Lüqian and Li Yuandu, then? Surely those two deserve punishment?” “Wang Lüqian is bound to suffer. Li Yuandu is another matter. Besides, with war and disorder everywhere and the roads closed, how could the court conduct a thorough investigation? It must wait until peace is restored.” Hu flared up. “Do you mean we are simply to let those two go unpunished?” he roared. He had never spoken to Gu with such harshness. Gu stared in astonishment, unable to answer for a long while. The embarrassed expression on his face was something Hu had never seen before; it reflected his own loss of control back to him. “I am sorry, Gu,” he said, lowering his head. His voice was much gentler, though it could not conceal his indignation. That indignation was not directed at Gu, of course. Gu felt both pity and respect for him, but would not comfort him merely by saying what he wanted to hear. “Little Uncle, I know how close you were to Mr Xuexuan. But we cannot act on feeling alone. We must consider right and wrong, and the likely consequences.” Hu naturally accepted that principle. At the moment, however, he could not see what those considerations meant in this case. If a man had been wronged, was he not even allowed to complain? What, then, became of the saying that injustice must find a voice? Seeing him silent, Gu went no further. In truth, he too was thinking only of consequences, not of right and wrong. While seeking news of Hangzhou for Hu, he had lately had much contact with official circles. He had heard many opinions on Wang’s death and the fall of the city. Most people sympathized with Wang, but some defended Zeng’s failure to help Zhejiang with great vigour. The arguments plainly reflected factional loyalties and hostilities. Wang had fought alone. His closest patron was He Guiqing, who was himself barely able to keep his head above water. In such circumstances, anyone who championed Wang and disputed the rights and wrongs would inevitably offend powerful sensitivities and invite trouble. Would that not be foolish? Gu knew that his own reasoning was commonplace and ignoble. Yet his concern for Hu was so deep that he could not help calculating the dangers. These considerations could not be fully explained at once; indeed, it was better that Hu should understand them without their being spoken. Gu believed that, in time, he would. For the present, the urgent tasks were to raise the hundred and twenty thousand taels and prepare the dispatch to the governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.

zh: 从第二天起，古应春就为钱的事，全力奔走。草拟公文则不必自己动笔；他的交游亦很广，找了一个在江苏巡抚衙门当『文案委员』的候补知县雷子翰帮忙；一手包办，两天功夫连江苏巡抚薛焕批给胡雪岩的回文，都已拿到了。这时，胡雪岩才跟刘不才说明经过，『三叔，』最后他说，『事情是这样去进行。不过，我亦不打算一定要这样子办。为什么呢？因为这件事很难做。』刘不才的性情，是恨人家看不起他；说他是纨绔，不能正事；因而听了胡雪岩的话，大不服气，『雪岩，』他凛然问道∶『要什么人去做才容易。』『三叔，』胡雪岩知道自己言语不检点，触犯了他的心病，引起误会，急忙答道∶『这件事哪个做都难；如果你也做不成功，就没有人能做成功了。』这无形中的一顶高帽子，才将刘不才哄得化怒为喜，『你倒说说看，怎么办法？』他的声音缓和了。
en: From the next day, Gu devoted all his energy to finding the money. He did not need to draft the dispatch himself. His acquaintance was wide, and he enlisted Lei Zihan, a county magistrate awaiting appointment who served as a drafting officer in the Jiangsu governor’s office. Lei took the entire matter in hand. Within two days, they had even obtained Governor Xue Huan’s written reply to Hu. Only then did Hu explain the arrangements to Liu. “Third Uncle,” he concluded, “that is how we shall proceed. But I do not insist on carrying the plan through. Why? Because it will be very difficult.” Liu hated being looked down upon or dismissed as an idle scion incapable of serious work. Hu’s words therefore provoked him. “Xueyan,” he demanded sternly, “who could do it easily, then?” Hu realized that his careless wording had touched a sore point and been misunderstood. “Third Uncle, it would be difficult for anyone. If you cannot succeed, no one can.” This unintentional compliment transformed Liu’s anger into pleasure. “Well, tell me what is to be done,” he said in a milder voice.

zh: 『第一、路上要当心——。』『你看，』刘不才抢着说；回时伸手去解扎脚带；三寸宽的一条玄色丝带，其中却有花样，他指给胡雪岩看，那条带子里外两层，一端不缝，象是一个狭长的口袋，『我前两天在大马路定做的。我就晓得这以后，总少不得有啥机机密文件要带来带去，早就预备好了。』『好的，这一点不难。』胡雪岩说，『到了杭州，怎么样向那些人开口，三叔，你想过没有？』『你方始告诉我，我还没有想过，』刘不才略略沉吟了一下又说∶『话太软了不好，硬了也不好。软了，当我怕他们；硬了又怕他心里有顾忌，不敢答应，或者索性出首。』『对了，难就难在这里。』胡雪岩说，『我有两句话，三叔记住∶逢人只说三分话，未可全抛一片心。』
en: “First, you must be careful on the road—” “Look!” Liu interrupted, reaching down to undo the ribbon binding his trouser leg. It was three cun wide and made of black silk, but had been specially designed. He showed Hu the two layers, left unstitched at one end to form a long, narrow pocket. “I had this made on the Main Road two days ago. I knew I should be carrying confidential documents backwards and forwards from now on, so I prepared for it.” “Good. That part presents no great difficulty. But when you reach Hangzhou, how will you broach the matter with those people? Have you thought about that?” “You have only just told me, so I have not.” Liu reflected briefly. “Too soft will not do, and neither will too hard. If I am too soft, they will think I am afraid of them. If I am too hard, they may take fright and refuse—or even turn informer.” “Exactly. That is where the difficulty lies,” Hu said. “Remember these two lines, Third Uncle: tell a man only a third of what you know; never lay your whole heart bare.”
